item.title: Anthropic's public S-1 puts numbers on its US compute rent: up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI, $125.2 billion Broadcom TPU lease, $44.6 billion Nscale, $41.3 billion Lambda
item.description: Anthropic filed its S-1 publicly on 26 October 2026. The filing says it agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI for NVIDIA GPU compute over terms into 2029, about $3.1 billion a month once all capacity is delivered (expected December 2026), cancellable on 90 days' notice after initial non-cancelable periods ending January and March 2027. A five-year Broadcom equipment lease for AI accelerators carries about $125.2 billion of rent excluding interest and is non-cancelable except on default; Anthropic may issue up to $42.0 billion of convertible notes to Broadcom to finance it. Nscale agreements total up to about $44.6 billion into 2033 and Lambda agreements about $41.3 billion into 2034; both accrue fees only on delivery, Nscale must use best efforts to obtain financing, and about $34.9 billion of the Lambda total can be terminated if Lambda does not secure the facility lease. First-half 2026 revenue was $16.3 billion and operating loss $693 million. Caveat: the filing leaves the total commitment figure blank; third-party totals (Yahoo Finance about $430 billion non-cancelable) are estimates. Country conversion: the largest single disclosed book of rented compute, mostly sited in the US, now has public terms. [Signal 70, Confirmed, via Anthropic S-1, SEC EDGAR, 26 Oct 2026 (primary); Yahoo Finance 26 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Meta launches a $95 billion equity financing plan for AI infrastructure: $35 billion underwritten now, $60 billion at-the-market from Q1 2027
item.description: Meta announced concurrent underwritten offerings of about $22.5 billion of Class A common stock (via forward sale agreements) and about $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred depositary shares, plus a planned $60 billion at-the-market program in non-voting Class C stock that is not expected to start before Q1 2027. NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom indicated non-binding interest in buying up to $5.0 billion of the Class A shares. Meta reiterated 2026 capex of $135 to $145 billion, said it owns data centers in 23 US states, is building four superclusters of more than 1 GW each and is on track to nearly double infrastructure capacity in 2026. It generated $97 billion of operating cash flow in the first three quarters and held about $82 billion of cash and securities. Caveat: the ATM program has no signed agreement and its timing, size and terms are not set. Country conversion: a US hyperscaler is now funding its compute build with new equity, not only cash flow and debt. [Signal 66, Confirmed, via Meta investor release 26 Oct 2026 (primary); CNBC 26 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SpaceX signs binding commitment for an Apollo-managed master finance lease covering about $40 billion of GPU pods
item.description: SpaceX's 8-K (filed 26 October 2026) says that on 24 October it entered a binding commitment letter for a master finance lease under which an Apollo-managed entity will buy and lease GPU pods and related equipment for data centers SpaceX selects. Tranches carry lease terms of about five to five and a quarter years, rent is quarterly in advance at one-twentieth of financed cost plus a fixed rate set at pricing, and aggregate principal payments are expected to total about $40 billion. Closing is expected before year end, with lease schedules starting in the first half of 2027 as GPUs arrive. Elon Musk posted that the deal had closed and that debt markets have almost entirely shut for companies without substantial non-data-center revenue. Caveat: the filing describes a commitment subject to closing conditions, not a closed financing, and does not name the GPU model or sites. Country conversion: US GPU capacity financed against an investment-grade, non-AI revenue base. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via SpaceX 8-K, SEC EDGAR, 26 Oct 2026 (primary); CNBC 25 and 26 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: UK Treasury previews Budget AI package: extra £60 million for the Sovereign AI Fund and £18 million for an Advanced Chip Design Academy
item.description: HM Treasury said on 24 October 2026 that the Chancellor will make AI part of next week's Budget, including an additional £60 million for the Sovereign AI Fund to invest directly in UK AI companies (adding Physical and Industrial AI), a further £60 million for Sovereign AI's R&D Procurement Scheme, £18 million for a new UK Advanced Chip Design Academy, AI chip design capability in Edinburgh, an AI Centre of Excellence in Manchester and £10 million a year to study AI's effect on jobs. Caveat: these are announced allocations ahead of the Budget, not compute capacity, and no data center, power or GPU figures were given. Country conversion: small sovereign capital, aimed at chip design and firms rather than megawatts, a week after Microsoft left Nscale's Loughton site over grid delays. [Signal 38, Confirmed, via GOV.UK (HM Treasury) 24 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SK Hyper seeks about $350 billion for the first 5 GW of a 15 GW South Korean AI data center plan by 2035
item.description: SK Hyper CEO Chung Suk-keun told Bloomberg TV on 23 October 2026 that the SK Telecom unit is in talks with big tech companies and financial investors to fund 15 GW of data center capacity in South Korea by 2035, and that the first 5 GW phase alone would need about $350 billion (about 463 trillion won) including servers and equipment. It targets a first outside round by end 2026 or early 2027, plans phased operations from 2029, and starts with a 900 MW Ulsan project alongside a 100 MW AWS facility, aiming for a 2 GW plus Yeongnam cluster and further GW sites in Chungcheong and the southwest. Chung put Korea's current data center market at about 1 GW and said the plan depends on drawing inference and training demand from Japan, Taiwan and other Asian markets. SK Telecom plans to invest up to 750 billion won in SK Hyper through 2030. Caveat: an estimate for a financing-dependent plan; no investor, term sheet or customer has been named, and the pace will follow demand. [Signal 58, Corroborated, via Bloomberg TV 23 Oct 2026; Seoul Economic Daily 23 Oct 2026; Business Times 23 Oct 2026; Hankyung 23 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Kazakhstan signs Firebird investment agreement as Firebird secures a US export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs
item.description: During Jensen Huang's first visit to Astana on 23 October 2026, Firebird signed an investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan at the Akorda presidential palace. NVIDIA says Firebird has secured a US export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs; the first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz, targeting commercial launch in Q3 2027, and a planned second phase would take Firebird's potential capacity in Kazakhstan to about 500 MW. Kazakhtelecom has already deployed 400 H200 and 480 B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty and plans more than 1,000 GPUs at Data Center Valley plus more than 1,000 Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region in 2027. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Kazakhstan-founded Higgsfield AI. Huang called the country a future 'AI factory hub for all of Europe' (CNBC). Caveat: no contract value, power source or financing was disclosed, and the second phase is planned, not committed. Country conversion: a named US export license turns Kazakhstan's Ekibastuz plan into licensed GPU supply. [Signal 62, Confirmed, via NVIDIA blog 22 Oct 2026 (primary); Astana Times 23 Oct 2026; CNBC 23 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Texas environmental regulator suspends at least 17 data center construction stormwater and wastewater authorizations and shuts its online permit portal
item.description: After Public Citizen and FracTracker reported that automated approvals kept flowing despite Governor Greg Abbott's pause on data center permits, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality suspended at least 17 stormwater and wastewater authorizations tied to data center projects and closed its online application system; applications must now be filed physically. TCEQ says all data-center-related notices of intent are suspended and that these automated notices do not authorize operation, though they are required before clearing land of an acre or more. The governor's office says no state agency will approve data center permits until the PUC, ERCOT and the Water Development Board have the information they need. Caveat: the count of 17 comes from the watchdog groups; TCEQ and the governor's office dispute that any permit was improperly approved. Country conversion: the largest US build state has paused the paperwork that starts construction. [Signal 52, Corroborated, via Houston Public Media 22 Oct 2026; Texas Tribune 21 Oct 2026; Tom's Hardware] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Humain and NVIDIA plan up to 84 MW and about 27,000 GPUs in Saudi Arabia, including 50 MW of Vera Rubin for an unnamed US client
item.description: At NVIDIA GTC Berlin on 22 October 2026, Humain (PIF-owned) and NVIDIA announced an expanded collaboration covering a multi-phase rollout of up to 84 MW of AI compute in Saudi Arabia, about 27,000 GPUs. Phase one is 14 MW of NVIDIA Blackwell HGX B300 systems, about 6,000 GPUs on Quantum-X800 InfiniBand, with deployment starting in Q4 2026 for Humain Cloud customers. Humain then expects 70 MW of Vera Rubin infrastructure, about 21,000 GPUs, from June 2027: 50 MW for frontier-scale workloads of an unnamed US-based client and 20 MW for Humain Cloud from July or August 2027, all on the NVIDIA DSX platform. The National reports the Vera Rubin phases remain subject to final agreements. Humain targets nearly 3 GW of data center capacity by 2030 and more than 6 GW by 2034. Caveat: no primary release URL was found at our cutoff; figures are from The National and Data Centre Magazine, which quote both companies. Country conversion: a second named offtake for Saudi export compute in two days, after Nebius at Oxagon. [Signal 64, Corroborated, via The National 22 Oct 2026; Data Centre Magazine 22 Oct 2026 (company quotes)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Google and Voltus expand to a 1 GW Google-funded virtual power plant across PJM
item.description: On 22 October 2026 Google and Voltus announced an expanded agreement to build a 1 GW virtual power plant across the PJM region (13 states plus Washington, D.C., about 67 million people). Voltus aggregates flexible demand from businesses and homes, such as smart thermostats, batteries and industrial assets, that cut use during peaks; Google funds it and participants receive bill savings and cash payments. It is a tenfold expansion of a 100 MW agreement from earlier in 2026, and Google calls it one of the largest distributed capacity portfolios deployed by a hyperscaler. The release gives no cost, timeline or link to specific Google campuses. Country conversion: in the tightest US capacity market, a hyperscaler is buying demand response at gigawatt scale to make room for its own load. [Signal 62, Confirmed, via Google blog 22 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: UK industry taskforce with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Cisco tells ministers they have about 12 months to win local consent for data centres
item.description: The Guardian reported on 22 October 2026 (exclusive) that the Sovereign AI Leadership (SAIL) taskforce, whose members include NVIDIA, Microsoft and Cisco, told the UK government it has a window of roughly 12 months to build a compact that earns public consent before US-style organised opposition takes hold. The submission asks for a national framework of recommended local-benefit terms for councils and mayors, including an indicative contribution scaled to site size, and for host councils to keep more business rates. It cites dry summers and rising energy bills as drivers of scrutiny. Action to Protect Rural Scotland says 15 community campaigns are already active in Scotland. A government spokesperson pointed to existing measures letting councils in England's AI growth zones keep all additional business rates. Caveat: single outlet; the submission itself was not published. Country conversion: the industry is asking Britain to pay for social licence before the build-out, after Microsoft's Loughton exit and NextDC's consent-driven delay. [Signal 58, Single-source, via The Guardian 22 Oct 2026 (exclusive)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: IREN secures grid power and a civil works license for a planned 300 MW AI campus in Badajoz, Spain, targeting 2028
item.description: At NVIDIA GTC Berlin on 21 October 2026, IREN announced it has secured grid-connected power and the civil works license for a planned AI data center of about 300 MW in Badajoz, Extremadura, with initial operations targeted for 2028. The campus uses closed-loop liquid cooling, is designed for NVIDIA DSX compatibility, and will offer managed AI cloud services for customers with data residency requirements. IREN also set up IREN Europe, chaired by former Banco Santander CEO Angel Corcostegui, with Roberto Purcaro as Executive Director for Europe. IREN entered Spain in June 2026 by buying developer Nostrum Group. Europa Press reports construction should start between late 2026 and early 2027. No customer, capex or GPU count was disclosed. Country conversion: Spain gets a permitted, grid-connected 300 MW neocloud site while UK projects stall on grid queues. [Signal 54, Confirmed, via IREN release 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Europa Press 21 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: South Korea's chip exports hit a record US$27.5 billion for 1 to 20 October, up 222.5%, 44.7% of all exports
item.description: Preliminary Korea Customs Service data released on 21 October 2026 show South Korea's total exports for 1 to 20 October at US$61.6 billion, up 105.4% year on year and a record for the period. Semiconductor exports rose 222.5% to US$27.5 billion and made up 44.7% of total exports, up 16.2 percentage points from a year earlier; computer peripherals rose 424.0%. Imports rose 42.8% to US$47.1 billion. The data are preliminary. Working-day-adjusted daily exports rose 65.9%, so part of the headline jump reflects more working days than in the same period of 2025. Country conversion: memory and AI server pricing is now the main driver of Korea's trade account, days before SK hynix (28 Oct) and Samsung (29 Oct) report. [Signal 56, Confirmed, via Korea Customs Service via Korea.kr briefing 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Yonhap 21 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: NextDC cuts FY27 guidance and pauses all uncontracted development after Jemena suspends grid works for M3 Melbourne; shares fall about 42%
item.description: On 21 October 2026 NextDC ended its trading halt with an ASX release saying Jemena Electricity Networks suspended parts of the 66 kV line works needed for the next increase in grid supply to its M3 Melbourne (West Footscray) data centre, citing safety concerns, community and stakeholder opposition and the lack of local council consent. Jemena does not expect to restart before February 2027, and NextDC now expects that supply increase in FY28. Later increases also depend on new transformers at the Brooklyn Terminal Station, which are now expected later than planned. The Victorian planning decision on M3 Stages 6 and 7 is not expected until 2027 because of the 28 November state election. NextDC removed the affected M3 contracts, about A$140 million each of net revenue and underlying EBITDA, from FY27 guidance: net revenue A$475 to 500 million (was A$615 to 640 million), underlying EBITDA A$245 to 265 million (was A$385 to 410 million), capex A$4.5 to 5.0 billion (was A$5.25 to 5.75 billion). All new development projects and land acquisitions are on hold, site sales will be evaluated, and the contracts allow service level credits and in some cases termination; NextDC is assessing force majeure relief. Liquidity was A$8.675 billion at 30 September and covenants are met. Reuters reports the shares closed down 41.7%, about A$3 billion of market value, the worst day since listing in 2010. Country conversion: contracted Australian hyperscale capacity stalls on distribution-network works blocked by local opposition. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via NextDC ASX release 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Reuters 21 Oct 2026; ABC News 21 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Humain and DataVolt sign a preliminary framework with Nebius for up to 50 MW at the Oxagon AI campus in NEOM, Saudi Arabia
item.description: On 21 October 2026 Humain (PIF) and DataVolt announced a preliminary framework agreement with Nebius for capacity at their planned AI giga campus in Oxagon, NEOM. Nebius would be the anchor customer, with a contemplated offtake of up to 50 MW, half of the first 100 MW now under construction within a planned 360 MW first phase. The capacity is expected to come online in phases from Q4 2027, and Nebius expects to deploy NVIDIA-based infrastructure. The release says construction began about six weeks earlier; the agreement was signed on the sidelines of NVIDIA GTC Berlin. The framework is preliminary and the release gives no contract value or term. Country conversion: the first named international offtaker for a Saudi build-to-export AI campus. [Signal 66, Confirmed, via NEOM / Humain / DataVolt joint release 21 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Amazon drops data centers on its $427 million GW campus in Loudoun County after resident opposition
item.description: Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on 20 October 2026 for a preliminary agreement ('Project Potomac Promise') that is intended to eliminate data center uses on the George Washington University Virginia Science and Technology Campus in Ashburn, which AWS bought earlier in 2026 (reported at $427 million for 122 acres). Amazon will convey about 25 acres worth about $65 million to the county, donate $5 million to the housing trust fund, withdraw its data center application and forgo legal action; the county will fast-track rezoning of the remaining 97 acres for housing and mixed use. The county says Amazon acknowledged significant opposition to data centers at the site. Final agreements are still to be negotiated, and one supervisor voted against fast-tracking the rezoning. Separately, the board deferred to 17 November a resolution to pause data center and substation legislative applications for up to 12 months. Country conversion: in the world's largest data center market, a hyperscaler has given up an owned site rather than fight local opposition. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via Loudoun County news release 22 Oct 2026 (primary); WTOP 21 Oct 2026; Washington Post 22 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent reportedly order more than 3 million export-compliant NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500 cards worth over $35 billion
item.description: Reuters reported on 20 October 2026, citing two people familiar with the matter, that ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than 3 million NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500 cards at about $11,400 each, a combined sticker value of more than $35 billion, mainly for inference. The sources say total orders from Chinese customers exceed 6 million, that NVIDIA told customers it cannot guarantee delivery, that partners may receive only 5% to 10% of requested quantities, and that NVIDIA indicated it could make no more than 3 million cards globally in 2027 as TSMC capacity shifts to Rubin. Samples are expected in December with commercial deliveries from Q1 2027. B300 cannot be sold to Chinese buyers and H200 exports are licensed case by case. An NVIDIA spokesperson blamed outdated US export controls and China's own import limits; the three buyers did not comment. Caveat: single outlet, anonymous sources, orders are not deliveries. Country conversion: China's demand for compliant NVIDIA inference silicon is about twice the stated global supply. [Signal 58, Single-source, via Reuters exclusive 20 Oct 2026 (via US News)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Wisconsin DNR settles the Vantage Port Washington permit case by agreeing to a statewide data center strategic analysis due January 2028
item.description: On 19 October 2026 the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Sierra Club and Midwest Environmental Advocates announced a settlement (signed 16 October) of the challenge to DNR permits for Vantage's Port Washington data center campus. The permits stay valid and the case is dismissed. In return DNR will complete a statewide Data Center Strategic Analysis by 31 January 2028 covering AI data center buildout, related energy infrastructure, alternatives and cumulative environmental effects, with public scoping and hearings; Vantage pays the preparation costs and DNR keeps control of the analysis. Wisconsin Examiner reports DNR will also prepare full environmental impact statements for individual data center proposals going forward. A state PSC report this summer found Port Washington plus Microsoft's Mount Pleasant and Meta's Beaver Dam campuses set to drive a 40% rise in statewide energy demand over six years. Country conversion: a US state adds a statewide review layer for future campuses without stopping the one under construction. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via Midwest Environmental Advocates release and settlement filing 16 to 19 Oct 2026 (primary); Wisconsin Examiner 19 Oct 2026; WPR] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Entergy Arkansas adds a second phase of service for Google's West Memphis campus, with Google paying for about $600 million of grid investment, a 440 MW solar PPA and 1,400 MWh of batteries
item.description: On 19 October 2026 Entergy Arkansas announced a second phase of service for Google's data center campus in West Memphis, Arkansas, which it says will fulfill Google's plan for data center buildings on the site and accelerate the ramp of the original project. Google will cover about $600 million of planned investment plus a power purchase agreement: a 1,000 MWh battery at Driver Solar near Osceola and a 400 MWh battery near Hot Springs (both expected online in 2028), a 440 MW (ac) solar PPA for the Big Island facility in Mississippi County, an expansion of the Galet substation and two new 230 kV lines to serve the expanded campus. The Big Island PPA was added after Arkansas PSC guidance; the commission had denied Entergy's earlier request to take that plant's output in September. Entergy says Google pays the full cost of the resources for its service over a 20-year contract and projects at least $500 million in new customer savings from 2028, on top of $1.6 billion from phase 1. The expansion still needs Arkansas PSC approval; expected in-service date is 2028. DCD puts the campus at 600 MW. Country conversion: a US hyperscale campus moves to full build-out with the tenant funding generation, storage and transmission. [Signal 80, Confirmed, via Entergy Arkansas news release 19 Oct 2026 (primary); DCD 20 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Denmark puts data centres last in line for constrained grid capacity as executive order 892 takes effect
item.description: Denmark's executive order no. 892 on prioritising capacity and refusing connections under grid constraints, issued by the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities on 9 October and published 15 October 2026, took effect on 19 October. It sets four priority categories for connection requests to the public electricity grid; data centres whose main purpose is network-based data processing, storage and related IT services sit in category 4, the lowest. Data centres needed for a critical societal function can qualify for category 1. When capacity is constrained, grid operators can refuse lower-priority requests that would displace higher-priority needs, and willingness to accept flexible connection terms is part of the assessment. Requests of 3 MW or more are handled in regional rounds held at least twice a year. This is a rationing rule, not a ban on new data centres. Country conversion: Danish AI and cloud campuses now queue behind households, electrification and storage wherever the grid is tight. [Signal 76, Confirmed, via Bekendtgorelse nr. 892, Klima-, Energi- og Forsyningsministeriet, 9 Oct 2026, Lovtidende 15 Oct 2026 (primary); Digital Watch Observatory 19 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Singapore neocloud Aolani signs non-binding letters of intent for up to 500 MW of AI data centre capacity in Malaysia from 2H 2027
item.description: On 19 October 2026 Aolani, a Singapore-founded neocloud, said it signed letters of intent to take up 500 MW of AI data centre capacity across multiple Malaysian sites, targeted to come online from the second half of 2027 and designed to Tier III. Aolani would supply the AI infrastructure, GPU deployment and operations; it projects committing up to 580 MW in Malaysia by 2027, up from about 80 MW committed in 2026, to serve hyperscalers, AI-native companies and Malaysian sovereign AI programmes. The release does not name the site owners, locations, GPU supplier or financing. The letters are non-binding and subject to definitive agreements. Country conversion: a demand-side LOI for Malaysian capacity, not yet a contract. [Signal 56, Confirmed, via Aolani release via Media OutReach Newswire 19 Oct 2026 (primary); W.Media 20 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: NextDC halts ASX trading over a delay to power supply at its M3 Melbourne data center and flags possible impact on FY27 guidance
item.description: On 19 October 2026 NextDC (ASX: NXT) asked the ASX for an immediate trading halt so it could assess the impact of a delay to the supply of power at its M3 Melbourne data center in West Footscray, including on the FY27 guidance it has given the market. The request says the board had not yet met to consider the delay; the halt runs until NextDC makes an announcement or until normal trading on Wednesday 21 October. Bloomberg reports M3 is partially operating, with about 42 MW brought online during FY2026 and a further 165 MW under development. NextDC did not state the cause. Citi analysts Siraj Ahmed and Howard Suen wrote that the delay likely relates to distributor Jemena pausing work in September on 66 kV lines through residential streets after resident and council concerns, and estimated FY27 EBITDA could fall by up to A$25 million; that is an analyst attribution, not a company statement. AusNet says power demand from advanced data center proposals in Victoria exceeds the state's existing capacity. Country conversion: an operating Australian AI campus is gated by distribution lines, not tenant demand. [Signal 70, Confirmed, via NextDC ASX trading halt request 19 Oct 2026 (primary, via ASX Market Announcement); Bloomberg via Energy Connects 19 Oct; AFR and Capital Brief 19 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Israel's Electricity Authority backs a 200 MW cap per new data center and about 1,000 MW of new large data center connections after 27,000 MW of requests
item.description: On the evening of 18 October 2026 Israel's Electricity Authority published the main points of new rules for connecting large data centers, as reported by Calcalist and other Israeli outlets. Each new data center would be capped at 200 MW. The Authority would allocate about 1,000 MW more to large data centers on top of roughly 2,000 MW already approved, about 3,000 MW in total or about 20% of projected 2030 national consumption; some outlets also report a further 300 MW reserved for defense and government needs. Grid operator Noga had received data center connection requests totalling 27,000 MW, about three times Israel's average consumption, and the Authority had frozen responses. Developers would post guarantees of NIS 2 million per requested MW (reported: half returned only once 60% of the capacity operates) and accept disconnection during extreme demand. Calcalist says requests for 500 MW and 1,100 MW sites would be blocked. The full decision goes to a three-week public consultation and may change before it takes effect. Country conversion: Israel is converting a 27 GW request queue into a capped, bonded allocation. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via Calcalist / Ctech 19 Oct 2026; Sektor; The State of Israel 18 Oct 2026; Electricity Authority decision summary (full text pending consultation)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Microsoft exits its anchor deal at Nscale's Loughton, Essex AI data center after UK Power Networks pushes grid power into the 2030s
item.description: Microsoft has ended its agreement to take capacity at Nscale's planned AI data center in Loughton, Essex, first reported by The Telegraph on 18 October 2026 and followed by the BBC, the Guardian, the FT and City AM. UK Power Networks had told Nscale the site would not get sufficient grid power until the early to mid 2030s, against a planned 2026 power date and 2027 opening, citing work needed on the wider transmission network. The project was announced in 2025 as the UK's largest AI supercomputer: Nscale pledged about GBP 2 billion, around 23,000 Nvidia GPUs were planned to serve Microsoft Azure, and Nscale has said the site could grow from 50 to 90 MW. Microsoft had said only last month that part of its US$30 billion UK investment would fund the Loughton supercomputer. A Microsoft spokesperson told City AM the decision 'relates to a single site' and that it remains committed to the partnership; Nscale said it remains committed to Loughton, is exploring alternative power sources and other UK sites, and that the grid issue has no impact on its other contracts. The two still work together in Norway, Portugal and the US. Country conversion: the UK's flagship AI compute site has lost its anchor tenant because of grid timing, not demand. [Signal 76, Corroborated, via The Telegraph 18 Oct 2026 (first report); BBC 18-19 Oct; Guardian 18 Oct; City AM 19 Oct (Microsoft and Nscale statements); FT] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Anthropic signs a 20-year lease for the first 95 MW of EverWind's planned 420 MW Point Tupper campus in Nova Scotia, its first data center deal in Canada
item.description: On 16 October 2026 EverWind announced more than $10 billion of planned private investment at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia: more than $8 billion to develop, build, own and finance a data center campus and $2 billion for four onshore wind projects (Bear Lake, Windy Ridge, Kmtnuk, Upper Afton). The campus starts with a 95 MW phase in late 2027 and a 325 MW expansion targeted for 2028, subject to commercial, technical and regulatory conditions, for 420 MW at full build. EverWind's release names only a 'leading frontier AI developer' on a long-term lease; Anthropic confirmed in its own release the same day that it will lease the first phase for at least 20 years to power Claude models, and Reuters reported it as Anthropic's first Canadian data center agreement. EverWind says it will fund all connection, network upgrade and other system costs attributable to the project, add several hundred MWh of batteries, design the campus to cut grid draw when needed, and not connect the expansion until system studies and approvals are complete; existing grid supply serves phase 1 at first. Closed-loop cooling is estimated at about 100,000 litres of water a day for phase 1 and 500,000 at 420 MW. About 2,000 construction and 215 permanent jobs are projected; a Membertou-led First Nations consortium is negotiating an equity stake (CBC: 9%). Land clearing is underway. Country conversion: a frontier lab has signed a binding, multi-decade lease for Canadian capacity behind a developer-funded grid connection. [Signal 78, Confirmed, via EverWind release via GlobeNewswire 16 Oct 2026 (primary); Anthropic release 16 Oct as reported by CBC News; Reuters and Canadian Press 16-17 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: NiSource GenCo signs a 20-year Microsoft energy agreement for northwest Indiana: ~1,100 MW new generation from 2028 plus 600 MW BESS, fully funded by the hyperscaler
item.description: On 16 October 2026 NiSource Inc. announced a long-term energy agreement with Microsoft for its previously announced northwest Indiana data center campus. Under NiSource Generation Company LLC (GenCo), Microsoft is expected to begin taking electric service on a 20-year term starting in 2028. The GenCo-owned pool portfolio will increase by approximately 1,100 MW of new generation resources, and NIPSCO and GenCo will provide transmission and generation infrastructure; Microsoft fully funds all generation and transmission required to serve its load. In connection with the agreement, GenCo contracted 600 MW of battery storage under a long-term tolling agreement with an AGP Group affiliate, added to GenCo’s multi-customer pool. NiSource says expected NIPSCO electric customer savings over the life of data center contracts rise to about $1.75 billion (from $1.4 billion previously disclosed), as much as about $140 per customer annually. Additional operational and financial detail is slated for NiSource’s third-quarter earnings call. Country conversion: a named hyperscaler load in Indiana now sits behind customer-funded GenCo generation and storage rather than a standard residential-rate pass-through. [Signal 80, Confirmed, via NiSource primary PR 16 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: CapitaLand India Trust launches CapitaLand Data Centre Chennai 01: 34 MW IT, 53 MW gross, about US$203 million, completion by end 2026
item.description: On 15 October 2026 CapitaLand India Trust (CLINT) launched CapitaLand Data Centre Chennai 01 in Ambattur, Chennai, its first data center in Tamil Nadu, with Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. The facility represents about INR 19.4 billion (US$203.2 million) of investment, will have 53 MW of gross power capacity and 34 MW of IT capacity across 13 data halls when completed by the end of 2026, and is designed for high-density computing including liquid cooling. It is jointly held by CLINT and CapitaLand India Data Centre Fund. CLINT's Navi Mumbai data center is fully leased to a global hyperscaler; no tenant is named for Chennai. Country conversion: another sponsor-built, near-complete shell in India's second data center corridor, launched at head-of-state level. [Signal 60, Corroborated, via The Business Times 15 Oct 2026; The Hindu BusinessLine 15 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Uruguay and Solaria sign a strategic FTZ agreement for up to 500 MW of data-center campus capacity plus up to 350 MW solar (US$5.7B cited)
item.description: On 14 October 2026 Uruguay’s President Yamandú Orsi signed a strategic agreement with Spain’s Solaria Energía y Medio Ambiente to develop a data-center technology campus of up to 500 MW under the free-trade-zone regime, together with up to 350 MW of solar PV on UTE land with a PPA envisaged for up to 40 years. Solaria will develop and operate the FTZ (land, infrastructure, services) and the electrical connection to Uruguay’s 500 kV grid. Development is phased: an initial 200 MW of data-center capacity (Canelones) then an additional 300 MW (San José), with solar concentrated in Florida. Uruguay’s Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mining cites a historic US$5.7 billion investment (about US$5.5 billion data centers and US$200 million solar), roughly 3,100 construction jobs in phase one (~2029) and about 1,500 permanent jobs at full operation. Binding contracts remain ahead (press coverage points to a May 2027 target). Country conversion: a sovereign-sponsored LatAm package of FTZ land, renewables, and transmission for operator tenants, not yet a named hyperscaler offtake. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via MIEM Uruguay 14 Oct 2026; Solaria corporate release] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: EdgeConneX and Stockland launch a 50:50 Australia JV with 450 MW secured for Sydney and Melbourne hyperscale campuses
item.description: On 14 October 2026 EdgeConneX announced a 50:50 joint venture with Stockland (ASX: SGP) to develop, own, and operate hyperscale data center campuses in Australia, starting with Sydney and Melbourne. The partners say they have secured 450 MW of power across the initial portfolio and are progressing additional power applications and planning. EdgeConneX appointed Chris Maher as Managing Director for Australia and joined Data Centres Australia as a principal member. Stockland’s earlier 3Q26 ASX operational update had already flagged contractual negotiations for the partnership and three existing sites with secured power totaling 450 MW. Country conversion: a new Australian sponsor platform enters with megawatts already secured rather than land-only optionality. [Signal 66, Confirmed, via EdgeConneX primary PR 14 Oct 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: AEP plans about $4 billion for a 702 MW Bloom fuel cell plant near Cheyenne, Wyoming under a 20-year Google PPA
item.description: On 14 October 2026 American Electric Power (Nasdaq: AEP) said it plans to invest about $4 billion in a new 702 MW fuel cell generation project near Cheyenne, Wyoming, selling the output to Google under a 20-year power purchase agreement. The project company, Cheyenne Fuel Cell, LLC, is about 92% owned and controlled by AEP and nearly 8% by funds advised by Basalt Infrastructure Partners. The plant uses Bloom Energy fuel cells, generates power without combustion of natural gas, and includes plans to integrate carbon capture. Construction is planned to start in 2026, with full operation expected by the end of 2028. AEP says the plant supports Google's growing energy needs in the greater Cheyenne area and follows the Google and Black Hills Corp. agreements effective 30 September (already on the Wire). Country conversion: a named hyperscaler now has a second, utility-financed firm generation source for its Wyoming load, built outside AEP's traditional service territory. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via AEP / PR Newswire 14 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Fermi discloses a binding 15-year, $6.5 billion TensorWave lease for 222 MW at Project Matador, Texas, backed by AMD credit support
item.description: On 14 October 2026 Fermi Inc. (Nasdaq/LSE: FRMI) furnished an 8-K fact sheet describing a binding 15-year phase one lease with TensorWave at Project Matador in Carson County, Texas: 222 MW of total power capacity including 156 MW of critical IT capacity, $6.5 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term, two 5-year renewal options and 2.5% annual escalators. Fermi develops, builds and delivers turnkey; TensorWave takes occupancy in phases from Q4 2027, completing in early 2028. Fermi cites power capex of $3M to $4M per MW of total power capacity and turnkey data center capex of $10M to $12M per MW of critical IT, and an estimated phase one project-level NOI margin of about 75% to 80% (non-GAAP). AMD signed credit support on 13 October; per the filing it begins only after construction is complete and rent starts on the final delivery phase, and it ends early if TensorWave or its guarantor holds an investment-grade rating for 12 consecutive months. Project financing is not yet closed. Country conversion: the first named, priced tenant lease on a behind-the-meter Texas Panhandle AI campus, with a chipmaker balance sheet behind it. [Signal 78, Confirmed, via Fermi 8-K (Item 7.01, Exhibit 99.1 TensorWave fact sheet) 14 Oct 2026; Fermi x AMD credit support release (Access Newswire) 13 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html
